blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: Attacker sends requests using any domain name → Nginx has no deny rules → Directly reaches the back office The same entry point as a previous Trojan injection attack - attackers bypass normal routing by using unregistered domains to inject malicious code

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: Scanner/spider probes the server IP Server returns a 404 page and version information, exposing the tech stack (Nginx version, backend framework, API format)

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: No clear warning when domain configuration is incorrect Server returns misleading error ('User not logged in'), leading to wrong troubleshooting direction and extended fault resolution time

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: Mitigation Effect

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: Configure Nginx default blocking rules (returning 444: silent drop) Unregistered domain requests are immediately discarded Zero information leakage — Attackers see only 'Connection refused'

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: HTTP and HTTPS ports are fully covered Unregistered domains are blocked at the Nginx layer and not forwarded to backend applications

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: Verified: Normal domain access is unaffected All registered business domains (client, management Back Office (BO), and VPN node API) are functioning normally

blocks.section: Business Impact - Server Security Vulnerability (Severe Legacy Risk)
blocks.text: This fix closes the entry point for Trojan injection attacks. It is a maintenance-level operation with no code deployment required, zero cost, and zero downtime. We recommend separating test server and production server security groups in the future to further tighten public access on test servers.

2. Mobile Bug Fixes Multiple UI + Error Prompt Bugs were found in the local real device test (April 9th), and Amy (QA) also reported additional issues Issues from the Taiwan team only surfaced on real devices and must be fixed before QA version release.

3. Production Environment Deployment Redis Hardening, MySQL Optimization (13.1GB Log Cleanup), Backend Code Merging and Deployment for Phase 22 The DEV environment has been validated, but the production environment deployment needs to be executed step by step to avoid service disruption

4. QA + App Store Approval Amy needs to test for 2-3 days, and the Google Play approval usually takes 1-3 days Skipping QA directly to go live is too risky - Taiwan team's lesson was lack of testing leading to online failure

Conclusion: The delay was two weeks to ensure quality, not because of development progress issues. All code is ready now, the remaining work is QA full testing, app store compliance optimization and production deployment

Sprint 2 Progress Report (Week 1): Arrowfish Release Sprint
Key Risks and Technical Debt

The Taiwan legacy system allows devices to register multiple times, resetting daily free quotas indefinitely, and can be automatically registered in bulk by simulators. If not addressed, as the scale grows, bandwidth costs will continue to be eroded by non-revenue-generating traffic, leading to a decline in paid user experience.
This Sprint established a five-layer protection mechanism (under review). Normal free users are unaffected and fully enjoy the daily 30-minute benefit:
Layer Mechanism Blocked Abusive Behaviors
① Device Dimension Quota All accounts share daily quotas across devices; changing numbers does not reset them Reset trial usage time for multiple accounts cycling.
② Device binding After reinstalling the app, users return to their original account and do not receive a new quota. Refresh trial eligibility after uninstalling and reinstalling.
③ Simulator detection Simulator environment check at application startup, directly intercepts registration. Automated batch account creation in the simulator factory.
④ Rate Limit for Registration Each IP can register up to 5 new accounts per day Batch Registration by Device
⑤ Account Limit per Device Up to 3 accounts can be bound per device Unlimited Registration per Device

I. Matters of Note
1 FFF Company Matters Update — FFF Company EU phone number registration and new payment channel processing are still being advanced by Roy, progress to be synchronized.

2 🔴 Compliance Warning - This week's audit found backend user_flows The table retains long-term ‘user × VPN node × hour’ usage records, conflicting with VaaS's no-logging commitment. It has been prioritized for Sprint 3 ( mod-efficiency Phase 12 ) and will be split into a new table. - Until this fix is completed, we should not promote the phrase 'no logs' as a formal statement. especially compliance materials during the launch of FFF Alliance. See Section 9.

3 Gap in Dedicated Line Renewal Experience for Existing Customers — New Discovery — After existing paid customers' dedicated lines expire, The system does not allow renewal at the same VPN node; a new dedicated line must be purchased instead. Rebuying will reallocate VPN nodes, disrupting customers' original IPs and routing habits, which is a risk point for paid user loss. Team Planning: Introduce 'Automatic Renewal Deduction' — Automatically deduct from balance or bound payment channels before expiration, Maintain original VPN node binding unchanged. (No re-purchase, no VPN node reallocation). The scope for Sprint 3 is locked and included in the Sprint 4 candidates , shared with the VPN node automation roadmap and FFF Universal Payment module to avoid duplicating efforts on two products. Business Value: Dedicated lines are high-ticket items; renewal friction directly impacts LTV; automatic renewals can simultaneously reduce customer service intervention and involuntary churn due to payment failures.

Three Major Achievements

Complete Repair of Exclusive IP Payment Workflow — Previously, due to legacy code defects in Taiwan, every purchase failed, resulting in zero revenue for the category. This issue was fixed and validated during this sprint; it will be billable upon release next week.

Balance Payment Card Stalling Fixes - Replaced external redirection with new mobile JSON API, returning results in 1 second. Approximately 15% of total transactions involve monthly balance payments; expected to reduce customer service inquiries and refund applications.
Subscription Renewal Dates Not Refreshing - Associated defects have been fixed together.

Five-layer protection mechanism - Device-level shared trial usage quota, uninstall and reinstall does not grant new quota, emulator detection, IP registration rate limit (daily 5), single-device account limit (3).
# Fingerprint Recognition Replaces the old ANDROID_ID solution with encrypted verification, which cannot be forged.
- Normal free users are unaffected; daily 30-minute benefits remain intact.
Fix for launch hang — New users experienced launch hangs due to inconsistent backend field types, which have been root-caused and fixed.
Three issues with trial timer — Sprint drift, wrong direction, logout zero anomaly unified as server authority.
Localization of error prompts — 「Api Exception」changed to clear Chinese (device exceeds limit / account locked / balance insufficient, etc.).
Fix App crash issues — Immediate update prompt crashes during upgrade have been fixed.
UI cleanup — Lottery pop-up layer overlap, blank list silent exclusion, inbox delayed read status, QR code recommendation share not displayed, etc., nine experience issues.
III. Improvement and Business Value
Performance improvement
Indicators Before After Business value
App size 99.8 MB 71.1 MB（−28.7%） Installation rate of low-end phones / users sensitive to traffic improved; download waiting time shortened by about 1/3
VPN node list filtering ~500 ms (500 VPN nodes) ~50 ms (10x) VPN node switching no longer lags, smoothness improved
Build time 6 minutes ~4 minutes 50 seconds (−20%) Save about 70 seconds per release; QA waiting time shortened
Database query count Approximately 20 times per user per minute ~12 times (−40%) Supports a 3-fold increase in user scale without additional servers
Read-write separation 0% (write database bears all) 100% client reads only from read-only replica Main database load reduced, writes more stable
Memory Leaks Approx. 2 MB per session Fixed No longer slows down on low-end devices for long periods of use; crash rate decreases
Stability Improvement
Issue Previous Afterwards Business Value
Stuck at Startup Occasional Stalls for New Users Over 60 Seconds Root Cause Fixed, Network Abnormal Automatically Redirects to Login Page Avoiding the 'Cannot Use After Installation' Bad Reviews
VPN Connection/Disconnection Crashes Occasional Crashes Three Levels of Deep Crash Risks Fixed Crash Rate Decreases, Customer Service Complaints Decrease
Timer Skew When Screen is Off Unified to Server Authority Increased User Trust in Trial Time Error Messages Without Meaning
Error messages are meaningless Unified to English 'Api Exception' Clear Localized Explanations User Self-Solving Ability Improves, Customer Service Consultation Decreases
Balance Payment Card Issues External Webpage Redirects, Occasional 'Processing' App Returns Results in 1 Second Eliminates the Risk of Duplicate Deductions, Reduces Refunds
App Upgrade Crashes Crashes When Download Link is Abnormal Friendly Alerts Upgrade path no longer fails leading to churn
Security / Fraud Prevention Improvements
Risk Prior to Afterwards Business Value

Abuse of trial quota Free reset time for unlimited device registration; batch registration available with emulator Five-layer protection Bandwidth resources concentrated for real users; expected payback conversion rate improves by 0.3-0.5 percentage points
Paid VPN nodes being exploited API returns all VPN node credentials directly Unauthorized users cannot access paid VPN nodes Differentiated value of paid categories is protected
Password brute force attacks No login failure count limit Five failed attempts lock out for 30 minutes Risk of account theft decreases
Device identity spoofing ANDROID_ID is easily forged Device fingerprint recognition (encrypted verification) Enhanced depth of fraud prevention

No logging compliance issues Sensitive information still recorded in some scenarios Most of the system and application layers have been cleaned up (see new findings in Section 9, Sprint 3, Phase 12 for details) Can only be formally promoted after compliance with 'no logging' is completed; also a prerequisite for the FFF Alliance launch

blocks.section: III. VPN node and Back Office Automation (The Biggest Operational Leverage of This Sprint)
blocks.text: During intensified blocking in China, VPN node replacement frequency rose significantly. Moving the full VPN node lifecycle from manual SSH to one-click Back Office (BO) operations is this Sprint's greatest operational lever—it shortens the window and also Eliminating 'Key Person Risk' (No longer relying on a single old employee to remember the correct command).
Live (Production Stability)
Capabilities Previously (Manual SSH) Now (one-click Back Office (BO) operation)

Install New VPN node ~20 minutes per node SSH → Install Dependencies → Apply Certificate → Edit YAML → Select Process Manager → Verify Heartbeat → Apply iptables ~30 seconds per node , enter domain + IP + name → Confirm

Reinstall and Recycle Blocked VPN nodes ~30+ minutes per node Manual uninstall XrayR / residual → reinstall → failure relies on experience ~25 ~ 60 seconds per node , Check "Full Reinstall" → Select Host → Confirm
Batch Upgrade Serial SSH per node; up to 150 nodes in a few hours Parallel up to 12 nodes + Streamlined Progress + Failures can be retried individually
Failure Diagnosis Flip through SSH output to find which step failed Stage-specific error codes + "View Log" button directly view systemd output
Reheal (Token Rotation) — Deployment of token rotation for deployed VPN nodes + Re-registration (to resolve IP changes / token expiration)
SSH Firewall Policy Deployment — Single node / Batch deployment with one-click application
Special Line Order → Automatic Inventory VPN node Binding Manual Assignment Main Process Live (Renewal / Re-purchase boundaries are still under testing)
Auto-release VPN nodes back to inventory upon expiration — Daily batch processing
DNS Automation (GoDaddy + Cloudflare) Manual record keeping Automatically create DNS records when installing a new VPN node
VPN node Health State Machine — Auto-offline and auto-online for billing_dead / temp_down / flow_cap

Renewal and migration to cloud signing process both require dedicated window research The same backend-compatibility constraints apply; in addition, developed but not yet signed Windows changes are accumulating in the repository
WoSign detailed explanation

Current signature certificate form: WoSign Physical USB Token (Physical Device Code Signing) — When the team took over, the certificate had expired and could not sign out a new trusted Windows installation package.
Research the WoSign renewal process and current costs (the issuance cycle for physical certificates typically takes 5-15 working days).

Migrate to cloud code signing. (Cloud Code Signing: Azure / GCP / DigiCert KeyLocker / SSL.com, etc.) — No longer relying on physical tokens, CI can automatically sign; however, a revalidation process (institutional identity verification 1-3 weeks) is required.
Windows end-of-cycle bugs that have been accumulated during the transition cannot be released.

Tasks to be done (in order of estimated time): Research the WoSign renewal process and current costs (the issuance cycle for physical certificates typically takes 5-15 working days). Migrate to cloud code signing. (Cloud Code Signing: Azure / GCP / DigiCert KeyLocker / SSL.com, etc.) — No longer relying on physical tokens, CI can automatically sign; however, a revalidation process (institutional identity verification 1-3 weeks) is required. Windows end-of-cycle bugs that have been accumulated during the transition cannot be released.
Side effects of cloud signing: CI can sign = Windows can also automate releases like Android, but the initial cost (validation process) cannot be omitted in the short term.
Real drag on rhythm (observed):
Each backend ticket incurs an additional +30% design/test overhead. — Engineers must run the compatibility matrix (v1.3.0 iOS curl, v2.2.71 Windows packet capture), not just Android usability.
More requirements meetings are needed to determine whether a change is or is not possible — Interface contract modifications need to be confirmed for impact on frozen versions first.
API versioning burden. — Some changes can only go through the new interface, and old versions cannot be modified. — Implicit cost of maintaining two sets of implementations.
Knowledge dependency. — The team must maintain a clear understanding of the behavior for v1.3.0 / v2.2.71 (internal audit has reviewed 38/39 interfaces' backward compatibility).
No backend changes have caused iOS / Windows failure in this sprint. — Compatibility discipline is maintained, but the cost has already been paid.

blocks.text: Coverage expanded by 4x while eliminating manual steps, resulting in a total time reduction to ~45% of the initial time. The speedup comes from streamlining the pipeline (decoupling build and release, reusing artifacts via SHA, path-based builds, incremental uploads to download station buckets), with the -51% improvement in fully automated Kotlin compilation coming from two independent lines of improvement that are not dependent on each other.
Code Refactoring and Readability Improvement
HEAD has fewer net lines of code than v1.7.38 10,000 fewer lines (−30,236 / +19,274 lines / 1,123 files)— the direction is Cleanup Rather Than New Additions 。

Remove dead code (historical baggage with no business value) : the utilcodex utility library (5 MB and 80 transitive dependencies, with only 7 APIs used); the Compose framework runtime (used on only 2 pages, adding runtime cost without value); the Samsung channel scaffold (never released); the Kotlin billing extension layer (an unnecessary wrapper); the unreleased prize-draw online-time design from the previous round; redundant device-ID initialization branches; obsolete data classes and unused observers; mobile heartbeat polling (replaced by the VPN node-driven design); and the merger of baseLib and proxyLib into app, reducing Gradle configuration complexity.

Readability Simplify Build Script Comments (from 430 to 370 lines); Backend Config Cache Changed to Single Atomic Pointer, Replaced Scattered Locks with a Single Line; Unified Logout Sequence Closure to Entry Activity; Synchronized Countdown Display Rules to a Single Owner, Eliminating Original Visual Jitters; Consolidate Network Monitoring Classes into One (Removed Two Old Implementations).

Sprint Cleanup of Translation Mess : At handover, the database contained extensive mixed Chinese/English content and ‘ [EN] / (EN) temporary placeholder’ rows, causing raw templates to appear intermittently in the frontend ( {{plan_name}} ). In this Sprint, the Backend Write Paths Added Language Gateways (Rejecting Incorrect Language Content) + Three Languages (zh-CN / zh-TW / en-US) Filled on 10 Translatable Tables Once + Historical Dirty Data Migration Cleanup. The Download Page Also Strictly Separated by Language Switching, Eliminating Mixed Chinese and English in the Same Rendering.

Data Loading and Initial Screen Experience ： Immediately display the actual remaining balance after disconnecting from the VPN (no longer reads the stale cache); The response from the synchronization / connection interface directly includes the balance status (avoiding an additional API call); cold start preloads only the minimum dependencies needed for the first screen (avoiding the 429 rate limit); the splash-screen and progress-bar decision tree was redesigned, using the native Android splash screen and an in-app progress bar for long-tail scenarios where the old design froze beyond 3 seconds; countdown data now comes from a single repository, with all former sources removed; ETag caching covers every API, replacing full retransmission with a 304 response; the countdown restarts immediately after an ad reward instead of waiting for the next 60-second refresh; and expired logins are silently reauthenticated rather than interrupting the user with a pop-up.

Key Observation

The farthest is the fastest - Vancouver (175 ms) 15 s vs Hong Kong (31 ms) 24 s. Conclusion: Geographic distance is not a bottleneck for Back Office (BO) automation SSH control flow is roughly 50-100 round trips, adding about 1.4 seconds of extra cost at 14 ms × 100 ≈ 1.4 seconds; this is a 0.05% relative to the total time and is completely overwhelmed by the difference in VPN node's local CPU speed.

The true factor determining speed is the VPN node's local CPU + whether it goes through ACME - Vancouver uses 2 vCPUs to run wipe + install faster than a single-core machine; Guangzhou also has 2 vCPUs but is slowed down to 44 s by ACME.

The French VPN node with 0.4 GB RAM did not fail (completed in 20 s) — demonstrating that the Back Office (BO) automated wipe-and-install process is not RAM-intensive and that the lower limit is below expectations.

Mainland China VPN node is the only one noticeably impacted by geography; — The bottleneck was ACME communication with Let's Encrypt through the GFW, not SSH itself. The Back Office (BO) already provides a local mirror for the sing-box binary ( apk.arrowfishadv.com — The backend has already configured a local mirror (apk.arrowfishadv.com) for sing-box binary to bypass GitHub lockout; ACME will still go through Let's Encrypt, which is an area that can be optimized next (see Section 10).

The distribution of our VPN node pool across multiple continents is acceptable — Nearby regional Back Office (BO) VPN nodes are not required; a single Back Office (BO) deployment in Singapore can drive full reclamation across continents in parallel.

Twelve. Business Impact

Window shrinks to minutes during China lockdowns for switch operations — One Back Office (BO) operation can complete the full batch within 5 minutes; cross-continent parallelism does not reduce speed.
Reused VPN nodes instead of being discarded when blocked Reused nodes instead of being discarded when blocked
Operator error risk is zeroed out — The only actions are entering the IP address, selecting the host, and confirming; there is no opportunity to enter an incorrect command.

Sprint maintenance windows can be canceled. Since single-unit operations take 15-30 seconds and cross-continent parallel runs of 7 units take 44 seconds, there's no reason to schedule night shifts. Routine VPN node maintenance can be done during regular working hours.

VPN node pools can be more aggressively globally distributed. — The benchmark proves that one Back Office (BO) deployment in Singapore can drive cross-continent VPN nodes in parallel; separate regional Back Office (BO) instances are not required.

blocks.section: ★ Core Business Security Transformation — Free quota changed from 'client-side accounting' to 'VPN node-side accounting'
blocks.text: At Handover The mobile app tracked time itself free time and then ‘tell’ the backend. Anyone who modifies the app or falsifies captured traffic reports can obtain unlimited free VPN access. This Sprint reverses the entire trust model: The VPN nodes (server-side) will time based on real traffic and report every 30 seconds; the backend is the only trusted source. 。

New findings in this sprint Device Quota Recognition Defects Connection Status Judgment: Currently, the judgment for active VPN connections is based solely on the device ID. When a new account connects to an already connected account, the session of the previously connected account is terminated. device_id When a physical device is used by multiple accounts, the latter account will terminate or intercept the session of the former account. The team solution: The connection status will be judged using a combination of 'account+device' identity —— web login does not establish device binding and does not consume device quota. blocks.section: 7. Why Technical Debt Must Be Cleared First — FFF Reuses the Same Back Office (BO)
blocks.text: Team's Solution: Do not build a simplified or renamed sing-box; instead, develop an original solution: a client engine. SkyTunnel No simplified or renamed version of sing-box will be developed; instead, we will invest in developing an original solution —— client engine SkyTunnel and a custom program for the VPN node side. This solution is completely independent from sing-box / libbox or any third-party open-source VPN kernel. The VPN node-side solution was validated as usable on 7/10, while Android client-side validation continues. In addition to addressing these two risks, both server-side and client-side code will be replaced with original code, eliminating the team's dependency on third-party open-source projects for version changes, defect fixes, or license modifications, thereby enhancing management and control. This self-developed direction also lays the groundwork for FFF to reuse the same engine —— FFF and future clients can directly use SkyTunnel without facing similar compliance and reliability issues.

blocks.section: Six. Key Risks and Technical Debt - iOS Client Compliance Audit
blocks.text: Based on this, the team conducted a comprehensive compliance audit of the existing iOS code, with the conclusion being: The current code cannot be directly resubmitted under the new account . Three structural barriers exist, all of which were issues inherited from the handover with the Taiwan team and not newly added in this sprint:

blocks.section: Six. Key Risks and Technical Debt - iOS Client Compliance Audit
blocks.text: Discovery Business Impact Solution

blocks.section: Six. Key Risks and Technical Debt - iOS Client Compliance Audit
blocks.text: 1. Authorization Compliance — Similar to the sing-box issue The existing iOS client is based on a third-party GPL-3.0 open-source terminal software, with 233 files containing the open-source license statement and no accompanying authorization documents. This is precisely the same issue that General Manager Ri on June 27 raised regarding sing-box —— there is a structural conflict between GPL-3.0 and App Store's closed-source commercial distribution. The difference lies in that while the problem with sing-box was preemptively avoided during Sprint 7, this debt from the iOS client was inherited alongside the handover. Remove all third-party open-source code and rebuild with proprietary code only. The audit confirms this is feasible : 162 files related to account, connection, in-app purchases, etc., are completely independent of the open-source code and can be fully separated.

blocks.section: Six. Key Risks and Technical Debt - iOS Client Compliance Audit
blocks.text: 2. Mismatch between Product Positioning and Actual Functionality The application was submitted for review under the name of 'SSH terminal tool,' with the store category also registered as a developer tool, but its primary function is actually a VPN connection. Apple explicitly prohibits applications from having actual functionalities that do not match their store descriptions. This mismatch itself constitutes an obstacle to resubmission and is related to the time when the original account was terminated. Resubmit under a real identity: Correct the store category, name, and description to accurately reflect the VPN functionality and used protocol. The application identifier for the new account has already been pre-registered with the name 'VPN,' aligning with this direction.

blocks.section: Six. Key Risks and Technical Debt - iOS Client Compliance Audit
blocks.text: 3. Core network components have no source code. The core network component responsible for carrying all user traffic is a 42 MB pre-compiled binary file provided by external personnel on their personal computers, with no source code or build scripts in the repository. None of its internally statically linked 76 third-party components have any licensing statements. The team cannot explain what is included in their application, cannot patch any of its components' security vulnerabilities, and cannot rebuild it. This is a supply chain risk, not just an authorization issue. Approach confirmed Switch directly to the team's in-house SkyTunnel Engine —— Sprint 7 planning, Sprint 8 has validated complete replacement of third-party kernels on Android and integrated the same engine into Windows. No external source code is required. , this risk is eliminated with the component replacement.
Positive audit conclusions
Sprint 8/7
# Task Item Objective
1 Remove all third-party open-source terminal code and retain only our own 162 files for reconstruction Mitigate authorization risks and remove a large amount of obsolete code and files

2 Replace the connection engine with the in-house engine SkyTunnel , connecting with our own VPN nodes. Use the same engine for Android and Windows to eliminate supply chain risks from external pre-compiled components.

3 Redesign the interface and operational flow, aligning features with the latest Android version. Ensure a consistent user experience across all three platforms; also ensure that store positioning matches actual functionality.
4 Validate the release pipeline using TestFlight and automated build pipelines. The release process is repeatable and traceable, independent of personal computer environments.
The complete technical details and item-by-item handling list for the audit have been archived in internal engineering records and are not expanded upon in this report.

Ten, Conclusion

Sprint 9 advanced both the 'delivery' and 'foundation building' tracks. Delivery end: Android passed Google's review on August 4th and is scheduled for release on August 12th; Windows delivery QA testing was conducted, and Siqo payment went live in the test environment. Foundation end: Attribution tracking for ads enabled linking ad spend to actual revenue for the first time; backend interfaces were streamlined by 30%, Android code cleanup was performed, build times for Windows were halved, and USDTPay error messages were consolidated into seven root causes.

The iOS compliance audit is the most critical finding in this sprint. Although the conclusion is that 'existing code cannot be directly released,' it has transformed an uncertain long-term issue into a well-defined engineering task. More critically, one of the most challenging issues — the core connectivity component comes from outside with no source code and cannot be rebuilt — Since the team decided to develop the engine in Sprint 7, switching directly to SkyTunnel now will suffice and no external support is required. . After the refactor, all three clients will run on the same in-house engine. The only remaining decision is the legal eligibility of the new account entity.

The key node for the next phase is the merge release window on 8/12 (switch to single machine integration at 4:55 AM, release Android version at 5 AM). The maintenance announcement was released ahead of schedule on August 4th. User-facing notifications are in place; jump hosts will be removed from the same window and replaced with Azure Bastion for accessing private VMs, addressing long-standing whitelist maintenance issues.

Production user quality, access eligibility and platform impact
Completing the full decision chain from takeover, backend quotas and device binding to China connection events, self-developed SkyNode/SkyTunnel, platform recovery, and FFF backend separation.
Management conclusion

400,347 registered accounts do not equal 400,347 real active users. The last 30-day VPN activity was only 4,938, with historical paying accounts at 19,476. The two most critical objectives post-acquisition – backend/VPN node authoritative quotas and device identity binding – are on the right track and have supporting traffic, sessions, and new cohort data.

Two major deployments cannot simply be described as successful. On May 25, production session accounting began and device identity improved, but user activation, paid activation, and traffic simultaneously declined; on August 12, infrastructure integration was completed and business metrics improved, but shared device identity showed clear regression. Subsequent deployments must be closed separately for product availability and regional acceptance.

Chinese events are not ordinary bugs: the same batch of test VPN nodes were available in Malaysia and Taiwan, but QA was unavailable in China. This prompted the team to develop self-researched SkyNode, SkyTunnel, and three reinforced protocols. Goals are ordered across five independently accepted modules rather than repeated by sprint. G1–G20 retain their stable IDs; G21 is the China smart-routing goal added on August 28. Goal Status Latest Progress Next Milestone Target Time
01 · Takeover, architecture, and engineering governance

G10 Full-system takeover, architecture mapping, and modular refactoring Core refactoring complete; launch contract in progress After receiving full production access in March, the team audited the clients, backend, databases, infrastructure, payments, and VPN node path; retired the old ProxyBackend; and reduced the API surface from 207 endpoints to 141. To resolve the coexistence of line v1, line v2, and bootstrap response formats, the standardized client-launch architecture is now locked around a catalogue, entitlement data, and connection credentials, using stable endpoint IDs to reduce duplicated compatibility work and connection differences across seven platforms. Implement the standardized contract, retire the old endpoints, and migrate Android, Windows, and iOS compatibly. Close the work with staging and cross-client connection acceptance; do not describe an agreed standard as a completed deployment. Continue through year-end Independent acceptance testing for each module

G12 Security, no-logs, and least-privilege governance Core fixes complete; boundaries pending closure Following takeover, the team fixed four no-logs policy violations, 13.1 GB of request logs, an Nginx attack entry point, JWT logout behavior, and OTP logic. Source-code access now follows least privilege, and staging credentials have begun moving to Key Vault. Close staging/production network isolation, SSH PEM access, production-secret migration, VPN node system-log retention, and periodic access reviews. P0 Closure alongside production resilience

G13 CI/CD, automated testing, and end-to-end observability Core system established Delivery progressed from manual packaging to automatic staging APK generation on commit. Android's four-channel build and upload is fully automated in about 15 minutes 52 seconds, backend pipelines were reduced to 30–50 seconds, and database-migration checks, MR quality gates, Crashlytics, and cross-client request IDs were added. Standardize build provenance, test results, signing, artifacts, deployment, and rollback evidence across Android, Windows, iOS, macOS, and Linux, and close the production-alerting loop. Continuous engineering standard Cover all seven platforms independently

G17 Production resilience, monitoring, off-site backup, and recovery Integrated and High-Risk Not Closed Read-replica use, the VPN node health state machine, and request-level diagnostics are established. On August 12, the application, MySQL, and Redis were consolidated in production. The final database backup is still on the production host, so host-level disaster recovery is not yet proven. Establish an off-site replica, perform an actual recovery drill, complete service and VPN node alerting, and record the RTO, data integrity, and cutback procedure. P0

G19 Traceable production release and user-availability acceptance testing Evidence framework established On May 25th, there were release tags and the first production session; however, Sprint 4 reports still referred to QA/preprod closeout. The deployment on August 12th and database restore can prove that product acceptance was partial. Record tags, runtime, DB migrations, product smoke tests, regional QA, and post-release KPIs separately. G13 owns pipeline quality; this goal owns the actual release and user outcome. P0 Prior to the next production release
02 · VPN core, VPN nodes, and network capabilities

G5 Automated Deployment and Management of VPN nodes Foundation delivered, closure underway Back Office (BO) now supports one-click installation, full-wipe reclamation, parallel upgrades for 12 VPN nodes, release on expiry, and a health state machine; two protocol issues received source fixes in Sprint 10, but end-to-end closure remains at 0 for the test environment, BO, and client, and automated supplier purchasing is not complete. Close out the agreements and Back Office (BO) acceptance testing first, then integrate the supplier API/controlled browser procurement into the same task loop. Sprint completion Procurement to Distribution Closure

G6 SkyTunnel In-House Tunnel Core completed Self-developed VPN tunnel core has been delivered; Android replacement verification is complete, Windows is integrated into the shared versioning core. Continuously returning and completing the official release of Windows and platform integration with Apple. Sprint Maintenance

G7 Sprint Completion, Full Rollout to China and Acceptance Testing Core completed, acceptance testing not closed Trojan, VLESS Reality, and ShadowTLS core implemented; 34 hosts ready for three protocols monitoring, 64 hosts still Trojan-only. External reachability remains unverified. Listening, full fleet rollout, Android／Windows regression, and China region availability acceptance closed; no longer covering four thresholds with a single 'complete'. P1 P0 Closure after Sprints of Acceptance Testing

G21 Smart routing and direct access to China sites Goal confirmed; development pending On August 28, Arrowfish adopted smart routing, which had previously been planned only for FFF. The goal is to connect mainland-China users directly to mainland-China websites and local resources, reducing unnecessary cross-border routing and latency, while other public traffic continues through the selected VPN. SkyTunnel and sing-box already provide routing, direct-outbound, and ruleset foundations, but no complete Arrowfish implementation, deployment, or acceptance testing evidence exists yet. Establish versioned China domain/IP rules and split DNS, and prevent public traffic from silently bypassing the VPN when rules are invalid. Verify Android first, then cover Windows and the remaining platforms and complete QA on China networks. To Schedule Not automatically added to Sprint 11

G8 Unbound Private DNS In Development Development of self-developed private DNS resolver ongoing; as of August 28, no integration and acceptance records have been made. Achieved realization, integration, and validation. Originally scheduled for August 2026 There is a progress risk.
03 · User eligibility, identity, and revenue protection

G14 Back Office Authority Quota, Timing and Session Core completed On August 29 review, multiple active sessions per account and device were all zero; the highest monthly traffic for free users dropped from 1,216.7 GiB in March to 39.0 GiB in June, with no one exceeding 100 GiB after April. A sudden drop in both activity and traffic on May 25th indicates that not all the decline can be attributed to quota success. Continue monitoring denials, expirations, replacements, free traffic percentiles, and user availability, and supplement Redis quotas with auditable snapshots. Continuous monitoring

G15 Unique Device Binding and Account Continuity New process effective, pending closure From May 25th to the following week, the device binding rate increased from 83.08% to 93.61%. Currently, the relooked shared device ID rate decreased from 21.73% to 2.59%; however, it rose to 38.89% on August 12th during the switch week. These ratios are based on the existing relationships as of August 29th and not historical snapshots. G20 Seven-platform simplified UI and advanced protocol mode Goal confirmed; development pending The latest UI supports Trojan, VLESS Reality, and ShadowTLS, but it replaces the previous simple experience of one option per country. Non-technical users should not be required to understand protocols. Add switchable simplified and advanced modes: simplified mode shows one option per country and automatically selects an available protocol at connection time.
